DF 53.16 Linux merchant-group chooser: native source reconstruction

Image: ELF:bcc6789e6fb477b785a2b02be80b8b1b054ff88c
Source: /home/lulika/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/Dwarf Fortress/dwarfort
Decompiler: Ghidra 12.1.2, DecompileCaravanPicker.java, imported disk image.
Instruction source: /usr/bin/objdump; original unwind ranges from .eh_frame.
No game execution, desktop capture or input is involved in this extraction.

elf-decompiled.c contains the six actual decompiler outputs. The six .asm
files preserve the complete procedures and literal operands. native-functions,
native-literals, native-calls, native-branches and native-switches retain their
original coordinates. native-productions reconstructs complete inline strings
and the name grammar; it is source material, not a runtime/check catalog.

The root renderer is 0xdcfe50..0xdd9ba4. Its choosing_merchant byte at +1
selects the pictured window. Its merlist begins at +8, scroll position is
at +0x20. An empty list draws only the heading. Rows are drawn in the same
native loop for unscrolled and scrolled lists; scrolling adds no text.
For each visible caravan, caravan_state+0xc selects its actual civilization.
The entity lookup is 0xd42ea0. The row consists of three consecutive draws:

  0xdd0cf2 / return 0xdd0cf7: capitalized species plural, caste=-1.
  0xdd0d30 / return 0xdd0d35: " from ".
  0xdd0d68 / return 0xdd0d6d: OriginalName(entity+0x20).

The species and name reuse rbp-0x80; the connector uses rbp-0x60. The
selected entity pointer is preserved at rbp-0xd8. The translation capture
copies its name policy, WORD identities and complete original-language
spelling while these native owners are live. A saved frame keeps those owned
snapshots rather than borrowing a stack pointer. The current grid/layer and
draw order determine which physical bytes the composite translation owns.

The species helper uses RAW plural NAME, rather than an enum containing only
dwarf/human/elf/goblin. Negative/missing species can leave the field empty;
the connector's own draw still supplies the row identity. Custom RAW plural
names use the existing scoped creature grammar and vocabulary.

OriginalName is not an English title. It uses native translation-table WORD
spellings in groups (0,1), (2,3,4,5), (6), plus optional first_name/nickname.
Group (2..5) is entered only if slots 2, 3 or 5 exist. Each nonempty group is
capitalized and joined with a space. Negative/unavailable language/WORD entries
append nothing. Nickname policies 0, 1, 2 respectively replace the first name,
insert after the first name, or replace the entire name. Unsupported game modes
use policy 0. has_name=false returns without clearing the shared species
buffer; has_name=true clears it before constructing the civilization name.
These are distinct branches, including a genuinely empty constructed name.

The complete translated row uses the civilization reference grammar, with
whole-field phonetic fallback for native spellings, and the scoped species
translation. Accented CP437 letters remain part of their native name field.
An offscreen native name is recovered from its owned original-name snapshot;
it is not recovered by splitting a visible row at spaces. All rows retain the
native selection geometry and use the available caption width.

The neighboring unavailable-trade branches produce exactly three existing
complete UI messages: "My apologies, but we're still unloading.", "We'll be
ready soon!", and "There are no merchants present with which to trade.".
The merchant's unit identity has its separate native designation formatter.
The chooser heading is "Select a merchant group to trade with:". All four
fixed messages already have authored hP translations; no per-word "from"
entry or world-specific civilization alias is introduced.

The complete root procedure also contains the later trade controls, 29-slot
talkline switch and item panes. They remain in this native extraction rather
than being mistaken for additional merchant-selector labels. Their authored
translation grammar is recorded in data/extracted/fortress-trade.
